Its individual strings are attached to the soundboard at an angle, and it is usually plucked with the fingers; it can be played sitting or standing. Most are made of wood, triangular in outline, some with several rows of strings and a pedal mechanism. It later spread to Europe, Asia and the Americas, and in the Middle Ages minstrels made the bardic harp popular in Europe. In the colonial period the Spanish Baroque harp reached the Americas and formed traditions in Mexico, the Andes, Venezuela and Paraguay. In 1720 Hochbrucker designed five pedals controlling string hooks, in 1810 Erard developed the seven-pedal harp, and in 1897 a Frenchman invented a chromatic harp, which became an important plucked instrument of the modern orchestra.
